**Status (2026-10-12): Design guide. Phase 0 is shipped for container runs;
Phases 1–3 are proposed.** Requested by the team on 2026-10-09: make
specifications, likelihoods, calibrations, and saved simulation sets aware of
which data managers (name and version) they used, including several managers at
once and different releases at different points of a process. This page fixes
the target design, its phases, and their acceptance criteria, so the work stays
consistent across sessions.

**Verified against:** jheem2 `dev`
[`85b73171`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/tree/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e),
jheem_analyses
[`08a250c3`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6),
and jheem-containers
[`39649e9f`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/tree/39649e9f50e20ff25adc53b691fdf61bbd7266cd).
Measurements are from shield2 on 2026-10-09.

**Candidate durable home:** the engine contract (identity, capture, recorded
inputs, comparison) in jheem2 documentation; loading and the release store in
the jheem_analyses and jheem-containers READMEs. **Graduation:** when Phase 2
ships, this page shrinks to a summary with links, and the adopted behavior is
recorded in the decision log.

Related: [reproducibility contract](reproducibility.qmd),
[manager selection and compatibility](manager-compatibility.qmd),
[SHIELD container pilot](shield-container-pilot.qmd#current-installation), and
[D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027).

## Goal {#goal}

The work is complete when these hold:

- **R1 Record.** Every artifact whose numbers depend on manager data records which
  manager releases it read: kernels (and so every simulation set), instantiated
  likelihoods, and calibrations.
- **R2 Identify.** A manager's identity is its content (a digest of the loaded
  file), with the release tag as a label when known. A manager changed in memory
  after loading is marked as changed.
- **R3 Detect.** Deriving something new from an artifact (rerunning its
  simulations, transmuting it, or starting the next calibration stage) compares
  the managers in memory with the recorded ones and reports differences.
- **R4 Declare.** A run's managers are immutable releases declared in its committed
  analysis code, so code and data move together and container and native runs of
  one commit use the same data ([D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027)).
- **R5 No behavior change.** Numeric outputs are unchanged, analysts take no new
  steps, and artifacts saved before the change still load and run.
- **R6 Several managers.** Identities are kept per manager, so a run that reads the
  census and surveillance managers, or different releases at different stages,
  records each.

Not in scope: changing scientific code or likelihood definitions; replacing the
existing references to manager globals; a general artifact registry; stopping
runs on a mismatch by default.

## How data reaches results today {#binding-points}

| When data is read | Example | Where the result is kept | Release recorded? |
|---|---|---|---|
| While analysis code is sourced | SHIELD likelihood instructions read national 1970–1993 totals ([`shield_likelihoods.R:229`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6/applications/SHIELD/shield_likelihoods.R#L229)) | In-memory instructions | No |
| Kernel construction | `create.jheem.kernel()` evaluates each element's value or functional-form function ([`JHEEM_kernel.R:156-160`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_kernel.R#L156-L160), [`SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R:5042-5108`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R#L5042-L5108)). SHIELD registers 26 such functions reading the census and surveillance managers. Kernels are rebuilt on every call; nothing caches them. | The kernel, saved inside every simulation set | No |
| Likelihood instantiation | Observations are pulled ([`LIKELIHOODS_basic_likelihood.R:929`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/LIKELIHOODS_basic_likelihood.R#L929)); outcome-location mappings read the default manager ([`JHEEM_outcome_location_mappings.R:143`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_outcome_location_mappings.R#L143)) | The instantiated likelihood, saved in the calibration's control file | Indirectly (below) |
| Calibration registration and setup | `register.calibration.info()` keeps a reference to the default manager ([`CALIBRATION_main.R:1576`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/CALIBRATION_main.R#L1576)); setup instantiates the likelihood from it (line 488) | The likelihood closure serializes the calibration settings, including the whole manager (line 608) | Only through the loader's attribute on the embedded manager |
| Deriving from saved artifacts | `rerun.simulations()` builds a new kernel from the managers in memory ([`JHEEM_simulation.R:119`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_simulation.R#L119)); transmutation builds a kernel for the target version ([`JHEEM_transmutation.R:326`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_transmutation.R#L326)). Interventions reuse the saved kernel (`JHEEM_simulation.R:2302`), but runtime quantity functions can still read globals. | Nothing; whatever is in memory is used | No |
| Analysis | Plots and analysis-time likelihoods read the default manager | Not kept | No |

Observed scale and consequences:

- **Managers have no content identity.** The object holds a name (for example
  `syphilis.manager_section3`, a build label), a description, creation and
  last-modified timestamps, and a code iteration. Eight methods change it in place
  and update the last-modified time
  ([`DATA_MANAGER_data_manager.R`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/DATA_MANAGER_data_manager.R#L618)).
  The analyses loader attaches the release tag and SHA-256 as an R attribute
  ([`cache_manager.R:89`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6/commoncode/cache_manager.R#L89)),
  which jheem2 never reads.
- **Code uses timestamps as versions.** Two SHIELD helpers branch on
  `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER$last.modified.date >= 2026-08-01`
  ([`shield_specification_helpers.R:138,202`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6/applications/SHIELD/R/shield_specification_helpers.R#L138)).
- **Globals are pervasive.** jheem_analyses has 845 references to
  `CENSUS.MANAGER` or `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` in 85 R files. jheem2 has no
  hard-coded globals, but 32 of its function signatures default to
  `get.default.data.manager()`.
- **Calibrations embed one manager and omit the other.** For a SHIELD stage-0
  calibration of one city, `global_control.Rdata` was 132.7 MB on disk. It holds
  the whole syphilis manager (2,471.5 MB serialized; the likelihood is 38.1 MB, the
  engine 42.9 MB, and the calibration settings without the manager 0.8 MB). Loading
  it took 9.5 s and about 2.9 GB of memory in every process that loads it. The
  census manager, which supplies population, fertility, mortality, and migration,
  is recorded nowhere in calibrations or simulation sets.
- **Releases change mid-pipeline unnoticed.** One city's native pipeline ran
  stages 0–1 before 2026-10-09 and stages 2–3 with the syphilis release of
  2026-10-09; only log lines show it.
- **A census update changes inputs selectively.** The 2026-10-08 census left the
  kernel's data-derived inputs identical for 18 of 26 SHIELD cities and changed
  only general-mortality coefficients for 8 (largest relative difference
  3.1×10⁻⁵) ([evidence](shield-container-pilot.qmd#current-installation)).

## Design principles {#principles}

1. **Data is an input, like code** ([D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027)). It is
   selected per run, frozen within it, and recorded, not built into a runtime.
2. **Identity is content; tags are labels.** A digest says what was read; a release
   tag says where it came from.
3. **Record where data is read, not where a run starts.** Most reads happen during
   kernel construction and likelihood instantiation.
4. **Capture through the manager itself.** Every read goes through a manager method
   or active binding, so instrumenting the class records reads made through
   globals without editing analysis code.
5. **Additive and backward compatible.** Saved kernels, likelihoods, and
   simulation metadata are non-portable R6 objects that carry their own methods,
   so objects saved earlier never gain new methods. New information is stored in
   private fields and read through package-level functions that treat a missing
   field as "not recorded".
6. **Report first, enforce later.** Differences produce warnings by default;
   stopping is an explicit option.

## Design {#design}

### 1. Identity on the manager (jheem2) {#identity}

A private field holds a small provenance record, readable through a package
function (`get.data.manager.provenance(manager)`):

| Field | Set by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | `load.data.manager()` | Base name of the loaded file |
| `md5` | `load.data.manager()`, using `tools::md5sum` from base R | Content identity, always available for loaded managers |
| `sha256`, `release`, `repository` | The caller, through a new optional `provenance` argument to `load.data.manager()`; the analyses loader passes its verified resolution | Release identity, when known |
| `loaded.at` | `load.data.manager()` | Load time |
| `modified` | `FALSE` at load; set to `TRUE` by each of the eight methods that change contents | The identity no longer describes the contents |

jheem2 imports no hashing package. MD5 identifies content for this purpose
(integrity checking of releases already uses SHA-256 in the loader and store) and
costs one extra read of the file at load. Copies inherit the source's record;
managers created in memory have no `file` or digest. Two records match when their
SHA-256 (or, failing that, MD5) agree and neither is modified.

### 2. Capturing reads (jheem2) {#capture}

- **Hook.** A private `note.read()` call at the top of each read method (`pull`,
  `pull.age.robust`, the `get.*` lookups, `unhash.*`) and in each active binding
  except the provenance itself, including `data` and `last.modified.date`.
- **Scopes.** An internal `capture.data.manager.reads(expr)` evaluates `expr` and
  returns its value with the provenance records of every manager read,
  deduplicated. Nested scopes all receive a read.
- **Where scopes open:** around kernel construction (`JHEEM.KERNEL` initialization),
  likelihood instantiation (`do.instantiate.likelihood()`), and the whole of
  `set.up.calibration()`.
- **Loaded, not only read.** Reads during sourcing (such as the SHIELD national
  totals) happen outside any scope. jheem2 also keeps a list of the managers loaded
  in the session, and calibration setup records it separately as `loaded`, a
  superset that covers source-time reads.

### 3. Recording on artifacts (jheem2) {#recording}

- **Kernel:** a private field `i.data.inputs` with the records read during
  construction. Every simulation set carries its kernel, so it carries these too.
- **Likelihood:** the same field; a joint likelihood holds the union of its parts.
- **Calibration:** `set.up.calibration()` writes `data_inputs.dcf` (base R
  `write.dcf`, human-readable) in the calibration directory, listing `read` and
  `loaded` managers, and keeps the same list in the calibration settings. Native
  runs get this with no change to launchers.
- **Access:** `get.data.inputs(x)` for a kernel, simulation set, likelihood, or
  calibration directory; `NULL` for artifacts saved before Phase 1.
- **Container runs** already record census and syphilis tags and digests in
  `inputs.json`; the jheem2 records let those be cross-checked.

### 4. Detecting differences (Phase 2, jheem2) {#detection}

- `compare.data.inputs(recorded, current)` reports, per manager, a changed
  release, a manager changed in memory, or a manager missing on either side.
- Policy option `jheem2.data.change`: `"warn"` (default), `"stop"`, or `"ignore"`.
- **Checked when:**
  - `rerun.simulations()` builds a new kernel: compare it with the saved kernel;
  - `set.up.calibration()` has preceding codes: compare current inputs with the
    preceding calibration's `data_inputs.dcf` or its simulation set's kernel.
    This would have flagged the mixed-release pipeline at stage 2;
  - transmutation: compare managers shared by the parent and target, and record
    the parent's inputs on the new artifact;
  - optionally, analysis-time likelihood instantiation against a calibration's
    record.
- A deliberate change proceeds and is recorded: the new artifact lists its own
  inputs and, for later stages and transmutations, its parent's.

### 5. Declared releases (Phase 0 shipped; generalized in Phase 3) {#declared-releases}

- **Today:** SHIELD declares its syphilis release in `shield_source_code.R`
  (`SYPHILIS.MANAGER.RELEASE.TAG`, line 44). Container runs use that declaration,
  saved with the run, and take releases from a shared, append-only store of
  verified releases on the NAS ([D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027)). Native census
  loading follows cached-metadata files with no release name, so container runs
  keep census fixed per installation.
- **Next:** declare every manager an application reads in one place in committed
  code (a short list of manager file and release), read by the application's
  source code and by the container wrapper. Census needs dated, immutable releases
  first, which is the census manager-build request. The native loader could then
  prefer the shared store over personal cached copies, giving one canonical store.

### 6. Names for managers (Phase 3, optional) {#roles}

`register.data.manager(name, manager)` and `get.data.manager(name)`, with the
current default manager as one name. Specifications and likelihood instructions
may declare the names they need, for preflight checks and documentation.
Moving analysis helpers from globals to names is incremental and is not required
for recording or detection.

### Manager embedded in calibration controls {#embedded-manager}

Keep it for now: for managers without retained immutable releases, it is the only
kept copy of the data a calibration used. Once every manager a calibration reads
is a retained release, setup can record identities instead and drop about 2.5 GB
of serialized manager from each control (132.7 MB on disk per city and stage,
9.5 s and 2.9 GB of memory at each chain start). Deciding when is an open
question below.

## Phases {#phases}

| Phase | Scope | Repositories | Acceptance | State (2026-10-12) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Container runs take the syphilis release declared in committed code; shared verified store; census as an immutable release | jheem-containers, jheem_analyses | [D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027); installation accepted with the declared release recorded | Shipped for container runs |
| 1 | Identity on managers; capture of reads; records on kernels, simulation sets, likelihoods, calibrations; loader passes release identity | jheem2, jheem_analyses | Gates below; new artifacts name census and syphilis releases with the loader's digests; earlier artifacts load and run | Proposed |
| 2 | Comparison and warnings at rerun, next stage, and transmutation | jheem2 | A rerun after a census change warns and names it; a stage whose syphilis release differs from its predecessor's warns | Proposed |
| 3 | Declarations for every manager (census releases first); optional names; store-first loading; decide on embedded managers | jheem_analyses, jheem-containers, jheem2 | Container and native runs of one commit record identical inputs for every manager | Proposed |

### Phase 1 verification gates {#gates}

- **Unit:** extend the [toy fixture](../toy-fixture-spike.qmd) with a small data
  manager and a value function that reads it. Check that reads are captured, that
  changing the manager marks it modified, that records survive saving and loading
  kernels and likelihoods, and that objects without records still work.
- **No numeric change:**
  - SHIELD kernel inputs for the 26 configured cities that build are identical
    with and without capture, using the comparison method of 2026-10-09;
  - fixed-parameter likelihoods are identical;
  - a short container calibration is bit-identical to one without the change.
- **Records:** a native `set.up.calibration()` writes `data_inputs.dcf` naming the
  census and syphilis managers with the digests the loader verified.
- **Where tests run:** jheem2 has no automated test gate. Options: run its tests
  in the jheem-containers CI, which already builds jheem2 at a chosen commit, or
  add a minimal workflow to jheem2.

## Rollout and risks {#rollout}

- **The team loads jheem2 from `dev` source.** A `dev` commit reaches every new
  session at once. Phase 1 changes no outputs and prints nothing, so it can land
  once the gates pass. Phase 2 adds visible warnings, so the operator guides should
  explain them when it lands.
- **Conflicts.** Put new code in its own file (for example
  `R/DATA_MANAGER_provenance.R`), with small hooks in existing files, to avoid
  colliding with active engine work.
- **Cost.** One extra pass over each loaded manager file (about 100 MB for census
  or syphilis); constant-time bookkeeping per read; a few hundred bytes per
  recorded artifact.
- **Compatibility.** Objects saved before Phase 1 keep their old methods and lack
  the new fields; the package-level accessors return `NULL` for them.
- **Analysis code.** Replacing the two timestamp checks with checks for the data
  they need is the analysts' choice; the design does not depend on it.

## Open questions {#open-questions}

1. **Mismatch default:** warn (proposed) or stop.
2. **Hashing in jheem2:** base-R MD5 plus loader-supplied SHA-256 (proposed), or a
   new hashing dependency.
3. **Where jheem2's tests run** (see the gates).
4. **Session-level `loaded` records:** proposed, to cover reads during sourcing;
   kept separate from `read`.
5. **Declaration format** for every manager per application, and how census gets
   dated releases.
6. **When calibration controls stop embedding the manager.**
7. **Store-first loading** for native runs, making the shared store canonical.
